text.title: Remote 1:1 Async Fallback Output Contract
text.summary: Draft-07 JSON Schema for `Async11Note`: one note per PM-IC pair per cycle in a two-person channel, with the recorded reason sync was infeasible and the consecutive-async cap, the three fixed prompts (blockers, decisions_needed, morale on the pulse axes), a 24-168 business-hour window counted in the IC's timezone, an IC-authored response or an unresponsive / paused status, a PM ack within 24 business hours with owned sprint-dated actions, the reschedule-then-manager escalation ladder that never forwards morale, and the quarterly response-rate review. Validator: `scripts/validate-remote-1-1-async-fallback.py`; staleness: `scripts/staleness-check.py`.

section.title: JSON Schema (draft-07)
section.note: What the validator's cross-field block checks beyond the schema: `posting.window_closes_at` is at least `response_window_business_hours` calendar hours after `posted_at` (business hours never close sooner than calendar hours) (r-response-window-in-ic-business-hours); an `answered` response has `received_at` on or before `window_closes_at`, and a `received_at` after it is `unresponsive` (r-empty-answer-ok-missing-field-is-unresponsive); `pm_ack.acked_at` is not before `received_at`, and when the IC reported a blocker or a decision (anything other than empty, "none" or "nothing") `next_actions` is not empty (r-pm-ack-within-24h-with-owned-actions); `unresponsive_count` is 0 after an answered cycle, `count_before_cycle` + 1 after an unresponsive one and unchanged after a paused one, and a paused cycle has no `posted_at` and no reminders (r-escalation-ladder-reschedule-then-manager, r-formal-leave-pauses-the-cycle); a paused cycle does not carry `sync_infeasibility.reason: temporary_leave` as if it were posted; `review.response_rate` equals `in_window_responses / cycles_in_quarter`, and `posted_at` is at most 90 days after `header.last_reviewed` (r-quarterly-response-rate-review). Whether `last_reviewed` is stale today is checked by `scripts/staleness-check.py`.

example.note: Subject violations: a 12-hour window posted at 17:00 Friday PM-time that closes at 05:00 in Warsaw, which is Saturday afternoon in Sydney (r-response-window-in-ic-business-hours); three generic prompts, none naming a ticket, a decision owner or the workload / autonomy / clarity scales (r-three-named-prompts-fixed); five consecutive async cycles with no sync call (r-async-only-when-sync-infeasible); a third unresponsive cycle with `action: none`, three reminders, and a manager packet that includes morale and the morale flag set to shared (r-escalation-ladder-reschedule-then-manager, r-private-channel-morale-never-aggregated-by-name).

antipattern.description: `sync_infeasibility.reason` missing, or `consecutive_async_cycles` above 3 with no `last_sync_call_cycle` inside the last 4 cycles.
antipattern.reason: r-async-only-when-sync-infeasible: async is cheaper for the PM, so without a cap it becomes the default and the relationship thins to a form.

antipattern.description: A prompt under 10 characters, "anything to share?" / "how is it going?", a blockers prompt without a ticket or WBS id, a decisions prompt without an owner and date, or a morale prompt off the workload / autonomy / clarity 1-10 scales.
antipattern.reason: r-three-named-prompts-fixed: a vague prompt gets "all good" and cycle N stops being comparable with cycle N-4.

antipattern.description: `response_window_business_hours` outside 24-168, `window_closes_at` sooner than the window's hours after `posted_at`, or a late verdict counted over the IC's weekend, holiday or leave.
antipattern.reason: r-response-window-in-ic-business-hours: a Friday-evening 48-hour window is "answer over your weekend" ten timezones away.

antipattern.description: An `answered` response without `authored_by: ic`, a missing prompt field counted as answered, or a reply that exists only in another channel.
antipattern.reason: r-empty-answer-ok-missing-field-is-unresponsive: "no blockers" is information; a missing field is silence, and the morale field stays in the IC's words.

antipattern.description: `ack_business_hours_after_response` above 24, or `next_actions` empty while the IC reported a blocker or a decision needed, or an action without `owner_role` and `deadline_sprint`.
antipattern.reason: r-pm-ack-within-24h-with-owned-actions: the owned, dated action is the only visible proof the note was read.

antipattern.description: `unresponsive_count` not equal to `count_before_cycle` + 1 after an expired window, `action: none` with an unresponsive status, count 1 without a sync slot, or count 2+ without a manager packet.
antipattern.reason: r-escalation-ladder-reschedule-then-manager: a third note into silence is the PM protecting their own calendar.

antipattern.description: A `paused` cycle with a `posted_at`, `reminders_sent` above 0, or an `unresponsive_count` that moved.
antipattern.reason: r-formal-leave-pauses-the-cycle: the reminder itself is a compliance problem in several jurisdictions and a trust problem in all of them.

antipattern.description: `channel.visible_to` beyond the pair, `morale_shared_outside_pair` true, or `manager_packet.includes_morale` true.
antipattern.reason: r-private-channel-morale-never-aggregated-by-name: the first named "clarity 4" in a leadership deck makes every later answer a 7.

antipattern.description: `review.below_80_over_4_cycles` true with `structural_decision: none`, a `response_rate` that does not equal the ratio, or a note posted more than 90 days after `last_reviewed`.
antipattern.reason: r-quarterly-response-rate-review: a pair answering 3 of 8 notes is not served by the protocol, and the protocol will not fix itself.

text.reference: Stdlib-only validator for this contract; `--self-test` runs both examples above.
Flags a note whose `header.last_reviewed` is older than 90 days.
Markdown note skeleton with the same header, prompts, response, ack and escalation fields.
